text: Hi, my name is Bunlong Heng. I am a Senior Full-Stack Developer, and I have been building web applications for over 12 years. I graduated from UMass Lowell with a degree in Computer Science in 2014, and throughout my career, I have always been the kind of developer who likes to own things end to end. I am comfortable moving across the entire stack, from React and Node J S to A P I's, databases, cloud infrastructure, security, and performance. I really enjoy understanding how the whole system works, not just one piece of it. Most recently, I have been working at Thrive. One project I am especially proud of is the Advanced Campaign Editor for the Thrive Business Center. I helped lead and build that application using React and Node J S, with backend A P I's, Amazon S three buckets, and support for themes and plugins. I also spent a lot of time working on the Reporting Center. As part of the Keep and Thrive integration, I helped plan the Reporting Center work for both Phase One and Phase Two. That involved understanding how data should flow between the systems, making sure it was accurate and secure, and helping break a pretty large integration into pieces the team could actually build and deliver. Performance was also a big focus for me. One thing I am really proud of is that we were able to bring our dashboard response time down from around five seconds on average to under half a second. I also worked on observability with Data Dog, created security and performance readiness checklists, and mentored developers around security, code quality, debugging, and production readiness. I am also A W S certified as both a Solutions Architect Associate and Developer Associate. But lately, one thing I have gotten really into is auditing. I audit repositories, P R's, Jira epics, portfolios, Git Hub profiles, and even projects that span multiple repositories. The project I am probably most excited about is something I built called Repo Audit. I wanted a better way to really understand a codebase, not just ask A I to summarize it. So Repo Audit reverse-engineers a repository across ten different engineering lenses, looking at things like architecture, security, performance, testing, maintainability, and code quality, and then brings everything together into one structured report. I have run more than 500 audits with it so far. But for me, the biggest reason I built it is to become a better developer. I can look back at decisions I have made, find mistakes or things I could have done better, learn from them, and carry those lessons into the next thing I build. It also acts as a quality gate for my work. Before I release or open-source something, I can audit it from multiple engineering angles and make sure the code I am putting my name on meets the standards I expect from myself. And as the A I models get better, the audits get better too. I can revisit older projects and discover things I may not have caught before. I think that represents me pretty well as an engineer. I love building, I love staying hands-on, and I am always trying to find ways to become a better developer and build better software. That is really who I am as a Senior Full-Stack Developer. Thanks for taking the time to learn a little bit about me.
